reason: DETERMINATIVE FINDING: New Zealand has NO equivalent of Australia's one-year domestic-fee cap for a second degree. I established this from the primary instrument, not from absence of evidence. The classes of persons entitled to be treated as if they are not international students for tertiary purposes are exhaustively enumerated in the Schedule to the Education (Domestic Student: Tertiary Education and Vocational Education and Training) Notice 2025 (SL 2025/325), which came into force on 1 January 2026 and revoked its predecessor. I retrieved and read that Schedule in full: it contains exactly ten clauses - diplomatic immunity; refugee/protected-person claimants and their partners and children; study under a New Zealand Government-approved exchange programme; enrolment in a Doctor of Philosophy programme at a New Zealand university; transitional TEC Industry Training Fund apprenticeships; Accredited Employer Work Visa holders on work-based Green List or sector-agreement study; TEC-funded search and rescue training; TEC English-language/adult education on partner-of-a-New-Zealander visas; and employer-required work-related training of 10 days or less. NOT ONE of the ten clauses refers to a second degree, a second qualification, a prior degree already held, a first year of a second qualification, or any time cap on paying domestic fees. The only study-concession clauses are the exchange-programme clause and the PhD clause. Consequently an international student in New Zealand who already holds one degree and enrols in another is, on the face of this instrument, an international student for the second degree and must pay international tuition - there is no domestic-fee cap and no first-year-only concession. Two important reinforcements: (1) clause 5, 'Domestic student status not transferable', forecloses the argument that a concession earned on one programme carries across to another; (2) the Ministry of Education's current guidance page (last updated 18 August 2026) confirms SL 2025/325 is the operative instrument for tertiary education, so this is the live position rather than a superseded one. WHAT REMAINS UNVERIFIED, stated precisely so the finding is not overread: the notice fixes ENTITLEMENT to domestic treatment, not tuition PRICE, and it does not rule out discretionary, institution-specific or scholarship-based fee relief awarded by a university - NZ universities do offer their own scholarships and fee-waiver schemes, but I did not fetch any university or Education Ministry funding page, so no institutional second-degree waiver is asserted. Separately, the ~NZD 10,000 per year domestic PhD fee and the NZD 56 million Crown subsidy cap that circulate in media commentary were NOT verified: they appear only in RNZ and other news snippets I did not retrieve, and the Subsidy is being reviewed, so no figure is claimed.
evidence_summary: Verbatim anchor from SL 2025/325 (fetched): clause 4 - 'For the purposes of paragraph (c) of the definition of domestic student in section 10(1) of the Act, persons of a class or description specified in the Schedule are to be treated as if they are not international students for the purposes of Parts 4 and 5 of the Act'. Clause 6 - 'The Tertiary Education (Domestic Students) Notice 2024 (published in the Gazette on 14 March 2024, 2024-go1042) is revoked.' The only enrolment-based study concessions in the Schedule are clause 4, 'A person who is in New Zealand to study under a New Zealand Government-approved exchange programme at a tertiary education provider', and clause 5, 'A person who is in New Zealand to study and who is enrolled in a Doctor of Philosophy programme at a New Zealand university'. Corroborating the instrument chain: Ministry of Education page 'Definition of a domestic student in New Zealand' (last updated 18 August 2026) names 'Education (Domestic Student: Tertiary Education and Vocational Education and Training) Notice 2025' as the current tertiary instrument; New Zealand Gazette notice 2025-sl7324 (fetched) records that notice as made 10/12/25 by the Ministry of Education under section 10(1) of the Education and Training Act 2020, notified 18 Dec 2025.
country_comparison_warning: Do not transfer the Australian 'second degree domestic fee' rule to New Zealand. In Australia the concession is a specific, named provision capping the domestic fee component for a second degree. In New Zealand the exhaustive statutory list contains no such provision. Any corpus row that lists a 'second degree domestic fee cap' for NZ would be a hallucinated import of Australian policy.
